Visit note | 2025-06-10 03:00 PM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Nazmul Alam, 32, male. Mr. Alam presents complaining of morning headaches, a high reading on a pharmacy machine, and occasional dizziness. He is a delivery rider and notes these issues started after a stressful month of overtime in Shyamoli. He reports no chest pain, shortness of breath, or visual disturbances. On examination: BP 161/92 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 57 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no murmurs, and lung fields are clear. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check his blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up in 1 month with home blood pressure readings.

Visit note | 2025-06-10 03:00 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Parvin Molla, 54, female. Mrs. Molla explains that she has been losing weight despite eating well, hating the heat, and experiencing a racing heart. She works as a beautician and first noticed these changes when her clothes became loose during a stay in Sylhet. She denies tremors, anxiety, or recent dietary changes. On examination: pulse 109 bpm, BP 116/79 mmHg, weight 82 kg. Thyroid gland is diffusely enlarged and smooth, with no tenderness. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid excess tea and coffee and rest when her heart races. Follow-up in 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.

Visit note | 2025-06-10 03:00 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Hasan Sheikh, 67, male. Mr. Sheikh reports experiencing dry skin and always feeling cold. He works as a shopkeeper and noticed these symptoms when a cold winter in Kushtia felt much harder than usual. He has a known comorbidity of Bronchial asthma, for which he uses inhalers occasionally. He denies constipation, weight gain, or lethargy beyond what is stated. On examination: TSH 9.3 mIU/L, BP 122/78 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 54 kg. Skin is cool and dry; reflexes show delayed relaxation. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep a regular sleep routine and eat a balanced diet. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH.

Visit note | 2025-06-10 03:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Jamal Gazi, 47, male. Mr. Gazi attends for review regarding his ongoing inability to raise his arm and persistent night pain in the shoulder. He works as a software developer and states the problem started after weeks of keeping his arm still following a sprain in Dhanmondi. He reports stiffness that limits overhead reach. On examination: shoulder lifts only to 65 degrees, BP 127/81 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 77 kg. Passive range of motion is markedly restricted with capsular pattern. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-06-10 03:30 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Tariq Shikder, 71, male. Mr. Shikder presents with more sputum than usual, a long history of smoking, and wheezing on walking. He works as a tailor and mentions his breathing worsened after a cold caught at a crowded market in Rajshahi. He has a comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies recent chest pain or lower limb swelling. On examination: SpO2 92%, BP 125/76 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 48 kg. Chest auscultation reveals diffuse wheeze and prolonged expiration. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-06-10 03:30 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Ibrahim Patwary, 61, male. Mr. Patwary returns for review of his chronic symptoms, noting they are worse with dust, accompanied by itchy eyes and a runny nose. He is employed as a garment factory worker and states his condition has been worse since road construction began near his home in Rajshahi. He reports experiencing about 8 sneezing fits a day. On examination: BP 112/84 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 62 kg. Nasal mucosa appears pale and boggy with clear secretions. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-06-10 04:00 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Sharmin Rahman, 79, female. Mrs. Rahman attends for a routine follow-up visit, reporting no other complaints except for headaches on waking. She works as a farmer and her elevated blood pressure was originally found during a free health camp in Sylhet. She denies chest discomfort, palpitations, or visual changes. On examination: BP 157/101 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 68 kg. Cardiovascular exam reveals regular rhythm with no added sounds. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up in 1 month with home blood pressure readings.

Visit note | 2025-06-10 04:00 PM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Fariha Islam, 37, female. Ms. Islam comes in for follow-up regarding gritty burning eyes, noting that her symptoms are worse in air conditioning. She works as a software developer and states the discomfort has been worse since night shifts at a call centre in Sirajganj. She reports using artificial tears with temporary relief. On examination: tear break-up time 4 seconds, BP 135/83 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, weight 82 kg. Conjunctiva shows mild hyperemia without discharge. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-06-10 04:00 PM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Dalia Sikder, 20, female. Miss Sikder presents with painful cramps in the first days of each period, accompanied by nausea with the pain, causing her to miss work or classes. She works as an NGO field officer and notes her symptoms became worse since taking a job with long standing hours in Chattogram. She has a comorbidity of Hypothyroidism. During presentation, she describes pain spreading to the lower back and thighs with vomiting. On examination: pain score 6/10, BP 122/70 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 58 kg. Abdomen is soft with no tenderness outside menses. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to use a hot water bottle, do light exercise, and keep a period diary. Follow-up in 3 months with the period diary.

Visit note | 2025-06-10 04:00 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Shakil Chowdhury, 72, male. Mr. Chowdhury attends for follow-up regarding worry about sleep, waking up tired, and trouble falling asleep most nights. He works as a homemaker and states his sleep trouble began after a newborn arrived in the family in Barishal. He has a comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies early morning awakenings or daytime hallucinations. On examination: Insomnia Severity Index score 19, BP 112/85 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 76 kg. Mental state examination shows anxious mood but coherent speech. Assessment: Chronic insomnia. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep fixed sleep and wake times, avoid screens for an hour before bed, and avoid tea after 4 PM. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a sleep diary.

Visit note | 2025-06-10 04:30 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Emon Sheikh, 77, male. Mr. Sheikh attends for a follow-up visit regarding a family history where his father had a heart attack at 55, alongside high cholesterol found on a routine test. He works as a farmer and his elevated lipid levels were found on a pre-employment test in Sylhet. He has a comorbidity of Bronchial asthma. During the visit, presentation notes highlight yellowish fatty deposits around the eyelids noticed by the family. On examination: LDL cholesterol 5.1 mmol/L, BP 110/84 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 83 kg. Cardiovascular examination is otherwise normal. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-06-10 04:30 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Asif Sikder, 69, male. Mr. Sikder presents with dizziness when looking up and nausea with the spinning sensation. He works as a farmer and reports his symptoms began after bumping his head on a rickshaw hood in Cumilla. He denies tinnitus or hearing loss. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the right side with torsional nystagmus, BP 133/72 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 89 kg. Neurological exam shows no focal deficits. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-06-11 09:00 AM | Dr. Farhana Kabir, General Medicine | Patient: Monir Miah, 60, male. Mr. Miah presents with severe aching in his bones and muscles along with a faint rash on his arms. He works as a schoolteacher and states his illness started after a week of stagnant rainwater pooling around his house in Banani. He has a comorbidity of Hypothyroidism. He denies bleeding manifestations or respiratory distress. On examination: temperature 103.0°F, platelet count 68000 per microlitre, BP 110/80 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 89 kg. Generalized myalgia and macular rash are present. Assessment: Dengue fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to drink at least three litres of fluid a day, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, repeat the platelet count in 48 hours, and go to hospital at once for bleeding gums, black stools, or severe belly pain. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.

Visit note | 2025-06-11 09:00 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Mehnaz Begum, 42, female. Mrs. Begum attends for follow-up regarding cramping belly pain, symptoms worse with stress, and stools that switch between loose and hard. She works as a security guard and states her condition began after a bout of food poisoning in Sylhet. She has a comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. During presentation, she notes urgent loose stools every morning with little pain. On examination: pain score 5/10, BP 134/86 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 83 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild tenderness in the left lower quadrant. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-06-11 10:00 AM | Dr. Farhana Kabir, General Medicine | Patient: Shyamal Halder, 48, male. Mr. Halder attends for follow-up concerning brittle nails and looking pale. He works as a graphic designer and noticed these signs after months of skipping lunch during long shifts in Narayanganj. He reports no gastrointestinal bleeding or shortness of breath at rest. On examination: haemoglobin 9.3 g/dL, BP 136/85 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 93 kg. Conjunctiva are pale and koilonychia is observed on fingernails. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

Visit note | 2025-06-11 10:00 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Anika Bepari, 78, female. Mrs. Bepari presents with symptoms that are worse when lying down and a sour taste in her mouth. She works as a madrasa teacher and notes her discomfort became worse since a job change in Dhanmondi led to late heavy dinners. She denies dysphagia or unintentional weight loss. On examination: BMI 30.7, BP 133/70 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 59 kg. Abdominal examination is unremarkable with no epigastric masses. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-06-11 10:00 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Tuhin Miah, 66, male. Mr. Miah presents with symptoms worse at night and numbness in his toes. He works as a homemaker and states his numbness has been worse since walking barefoot at home in Mirpur. He denies motor weakness or balance issues. On examination: reduced sensation at 7 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 126/84 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 96 kg. Ankle reflexes are diminished bilaterally. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to check his feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep his blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-06-11 10:00 AM | Dr. Towhid Alam, ENT | Patient: Rahima Munshi, 50, female. Mrs. Munshi attends for a follow-up visit regarding a blocked ear after a cold, mild fever, and muffled hearing. She works as a rickshaw puller and reports her symptoms started after a flight to Narayanganj. She denies severe otalgia or otorrhea. On examination: temperature 100.1°F, BP 133/74 mmHg, pulse 98 bpm, weight 75 kg. Otoscopy shows an injected and retracted tympanic membrane with decreased mobility. Assessment: Acute otitis media. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep the ear dry and avoid inserting cotton buds. Follow-up in 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-06-11 10:00 AM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Faruk Sarkar, 59, male. Mr. Sarkar attends for follow-up concerning constant worry for months and poor sleep. He works as a ride-share driver and states his anxiety has been worse since a family business loss in Mirpur. He has a comorbidity of Essential hypertension. He denies panic attacks or suicidal ideation. On examination: GAD-7 score 18, BP 151/87 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 51 kg. Patient appears tense with worried affect. Assessment: Generalized anxiety disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to practise slow breathing daily, reduce tea and coffee, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-06-11 10:30 AM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Shahana Pramanik, 59, female. Visit note | 2025-06-11 10:30 AM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Obaidul Bhuiyan, 30, male. Mr. Bhuiyan presents with both eyes affected and itchy watery red eyes. Visit note | 2025-06-11 11:00 AM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Liton Pramanik, 19, male. Mr. Pramanik presents with a twisted ankle and pain when walking.
